content: Do not share linezolid with others, even if they have the same condition as you, as it may cause harm to them. Always store linezolid out of the reach of children. When using the oral liquid form, do not shake the bottle. Instead, invert the bottle 3 to 5 times before measuring each dose. Use a precise measuring device to ensure accurate dosing; household spoons are not reliable and may lead to incorrect dosing. Consult your pharmacist for an appropriate measuring device. Before starting linezolid, inform your healthcare provider about all your medical conditions and any medications you are taking, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements. This information helps your provider determine if linezolid is suitable for you. Specifically, disclose if you have any of the following conditions: diabetes, thyroid problems, uncontrolled high blood pressure, a history of seizures or epilepsy, kidney or liver issues, low white blood cell or platelet counts, anemia, phenylketonuria (if using the oral liquid), carcinoid syndrome, or a tumor in your adrenal gland (pheochromocytoma). If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider, as it is not known how linezolid may affect pregnancy or an unborn baby. Your provider will advise whether you should take linezolid during pregnancy. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, let your provider know, as linezolid passes into breast milk. While taking linezolid, avoid consuming large amounts of foods or drinks high in tyramine, such as aged cheeses, sauerkraut, pickled foods, tap beer, soy sauce, red wine, and smoked meats. It is unclear if alcohol consumption affects linezolid, so consult your provider for guidance. Always inform your healthcare provider about any medications you are taking, especially if you are using the following: cold remedies or decongestants containing pseudoephedrine, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) taken within the past two weeks, diabetes medications, tricyclic antidepressants, bupropion (even if not used for depression), triptans (e.g., sumatriptan, eletriptan) for migraines, buspirone for anxiety, or opioids such as morphine or meperidine. If you or someone else accidentally takes too much linezolid, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of linezolid, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the entire prescribed course of linezolid, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to reduce the risk of developing antibiotic-resistant infections in the future.
